articleTitle: Tidal Becomes First Streaming Platform to Ban Fully AI‑Generated Music

sources.title: Tidal Becomes First Streaming Service to Ban AI Music From Its Platform - Billboard
Tidal is banning fully AI-generated music. Here's how Spotify and Apple Music compare.
Tidal Will Remove Wholly AI-Generated Music From Its Service - findarticles.com
Tidal Is the First Streaming Service to Ban AI Music - Rolling Stone

claims.claim: Tidal announced that it will delete any music that distributors confirm was created solely with artificial‑intelligence tools.
claims.bestSource: Tidal Becomes First Streaming Service to Ban AI Music From Its Platform - Billboard
claims.evidence: Tidal says that it will remove any songs that distributors say were created solely with AI tools, and it will also use its partnership with Ircam Amplify, a French AI music detection tool, to help implement the policy.
claims.bestPassage: Tidal says that it will remove any songs that distributors say were created solely with AI tools, and it will also use its partnership with Ircam Amplify, a French AI music detection tool, to help implement the policy.

claims.claim: The decision follows the service’s earlier practice of labeling AI‑generated tracks and cutting royalty payments for those releases.
claims.bestSource: Tidal is banning fully AI-generated music. Here's how Spotify and Apple Music compare.
claims.evidence: TIDAL will continue to make decisions that support real artists first," Andersen wrote in a post on X. (DSP stands for digital service provider, which is a platform that streams or sells music — like Spotify, Apple Music, or Deezer.) Tidal started labeling tracks as "wholly" AI-generated and cutting off royalties back in July. As Variety reported at the time, the service said it would label AI-generated music, deny it royalty payments and block or remove material connected to fraud. As Anderson noted on X, this decision makes Tidal the first digital streaming platform to ban AI music , and he pointedly encouraged others in the industry to “follow suit.” The move comes after Tidal began labeling and demonetizing AI-generated tracks over the summer.

claims.claim: The change removes a category of tracks that could compete with human artists for streams and royalties.
claims.bestSource: Tidal Is the First Streaming Service to Ban AI Music - Rolling Stone
claims.evidence: While much of it goes unnoticed — Tidal estimated 96 percent of the AI songs it’s already flagged have garnered zero streams over the last 90 days — tracks that do catch on can divert streams and royalties from working artists. TIDAL will continue to make decisions that support real artists first," Andersen wrote in a post on X. Tidal started labeling tracks as "wholly" AI-generated and cutting off royalties back in July. The change moves Tidal beyond an earlier system that labeled AI-generated material and made it ineligible for royalties.
